hook.text: The only thing connecting your car to the road is four small patches of rubber—about a handprint each.

buildup.text: Tire grip depends on rubber compound, tread pattern, temperature, and road surface.

discovery.text: Soft rubber grips better but wears faster. Hard rubber lasts longer but slips in the cold.

twist.text: A tire slightly slipping—around 10%—actually produces more grip than a fully stuck one.

climax.text: That's why ABS, traction control, and stability systems all manage tiny amounts of wheel slip.

punchline.text: Everything a car does starts at four hand-sized patches.
